broader_coverage.evidence: Dreyfus 2014 gives an algorithm plus integrability criterion for the Zariski-dense case; Arreche thesis/ISSAC extends it to triangular/dihedral and r1!=0. Both are conditional methods. No theorem states that every even-degree polynomial potential, or every quartic x^4+tx^2+c, has classical group SL2 or is non-isomonodromic; specializations (e.g. multiple-root cases) can differ and are excluded here.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A broader method paper does not cover the claim as a special case because its conclusion is conditional on hypotheses (classical SL2, rational unsolvability of the instance b-equation) that still had to be verified for q=x^4+tx^2+1. The draft supplies exactly that missing verification, so broader coverage does not imply the headline.
